explanation: Pointing at objects or directions with your index finger is unremarkable in the UK, but pointing your finger directly at a person - especially while making a point in an argument - can come across as aggressive or accusatory. Many Britons will use an open hand or a nod instead when gesturing toward someone, particularly during a disagreement.
local_tip: Point at things freely, but gesture toward a person with an open hand or a nod rather than a jabbing index finger.

also_check.note: Pointing at a person with the index finger is considered impolite; an open hand is used instead.
Pointing with the index finger is considered offensive; the thumb is often used instead.
Similar to the UK, pointing at objects is fine but pointing at a person can seem confrontational.
